design: G4 shared funnel and seam roller; original trough and holder
training_method: Begin with parameter search over a visually targeted joint-actuated pusher pickup controller. Collect successful demonstrations only after independent complete-sequence scoring and negative controls. No neural policy trained yet.

stages.task: Measure station and validate printed fits manually
done_when: Recorded base origins, table height/edge, camera intrinsics/extrinsics, staging locations and uncertainty
Carrier slides through G4 guide into original holder without force
Actual paper offset/yaw feeding, withdrawal and dry/damp folding tests logged
Measured grasp, insertion and stopping limits exist

stages.task: Visual registration and G4 pusher contact pickup, lift, hold, lower, release
stages.latest_evidence: Repaired pusher controller passes nine development placements, six fresh confirmations and eighteen solver repeats; matched nominal passes and all eight faults fail. Independent raw rescoring agrees. Historical v3 passes with late capture remain invalid for clean retention. No policy export or physical qualification.
done_when: 8 fitting and 3 independent validation poses pass; absolute simulator errors separately reported
No initial intersection; all commands through original SO101 joints/limits
Opposed loaded grip established before lift and retained through lift, hold and lowering until intended support
Whole-tool slip measured from established grasp; no unintended loaded arm/fixture collisions
Continuous two-jaw retention and clearance over 2 seconds; release free on rest for 1 second
Held-out offsets/noise and all negative controls discriminate success/failure
1ms/2ms and NoSlip on/off sensitivity reported
limits: One-arm isolated bench; not full cart
Yaw-fixed staging with tested xy offsets through plus/minus 8mm; no claim over all intervening poses or arbitrary orientation
40mm raised staging rest with near edge389mm; physical fixture unvalidated
Tag31 hypothetical 18mm black square on pusher
1920x1440 rectified rendering and0.8mm depth noise are benchmark assumptions, not an actual-camera accuracy claim
Ground-truth contact aborts are diagnostic, not deployable sensing

done_when: Both SO101 arms and actual station geometry included
Free rigid parts held only by jaw contacts
Fixture explicitly modeled and anchored as built
Original part seats and remains after complete release; no convex hull closes a cavity
stages.latest_evidence: A full rigid station now compiles both SO101 arm hierarchies and free original trough/holder/guide, four carriers, pusher and passive roller. Current diagnostic starts with human-prepared holder in trough, so it earns no credit for robot trough or holder placement. Guide transfer is under development. Station dimensions and printed material properties remain explicit assumptions.

stages.task: Four empty carriers through shared guide
stages.latest_evidence: A source-derived continuous holder-wall cover removes large artificial partition contacts. Conditional near-seat release cases pass, but the corrected model fails half-timestep, height, strong-friction and full-funnel-release checks under unchanged gates. Contact-normal approximation limits remain documented. No robot insertion or four-carrier success.
done_when: Collision decomposition preserves all four guide holes and 0.4mm carrier rims
Contact surfaces and normals agree with source exterior within declared tested numerical bounds, beyond global volume and opening probes
Gravity seats each carrier without snapping, forcing or object-pose actions
Offset/yaw/friction sensitivity and initial intersections audited
All four seated after release
diagnostic_limits: Only first funnel corridor has static collision geometry
Guide and original holder fixed by hypothetical fixture
Carrier reset pose and evaluator use privileged geometry
No robot, grasp/release, perception, trough or paper in this diagnostic
Audited hollow CAD alone does not establish gravity seating
stages.full_station_geometry_evidence: New reusable full collision bundle covers all four guide and holder corridors, audited against original source and local probes. It remains distinct from the previous single-corridor diagnostic; full-scene dynamics and all-four robot insertion are not yet established.

stages.task: Feed four real-paper strips and withdraw pusher
done_when: Measured thickness, bending, friction, damping and dry/damp response
Passive deformable-paper approximation has manual-test agreement
Rim catches, buckling and resistance cause stop
Pusher withdrawal does not drag paper or lift carrier

stages.task: Lift shared guide at least 28mm and park
done_when: Actual joint trajectories, both grips, 28mm vertical clearance
All four paper tails and carriers retained after release and parking

stages.task: Seam roller folds four strips toward +X, rightmost first
done_when: Purchased M5 axle/retention modeled and wheel rotates freely
Passive wheel driven only by contact, not a folding actuator
Lift between strips, proceed leftwards
No tear, wrap, tail extraction or forced jam
Hands-off retention under stronger springback and timestep/solver changes
Matched claw/pusher/roller comparison uses same paper, station and scoring
stages.mechanism_evidence: Actual G4 wheel/fork CAD and a passive ideal-axle hinge are implemented. A constrained mechanism bench rolls over a rigid 46mm coupon at both tested timesteps; zero friction, locked bearing and disabled initial motion reject. Earlier 0.4mm drop fails penetration gate. This is not robot rolling, paper folding, or validated axle hardware.

done_when: Validated paper grasp/release method
Full rectangle without notches
Paper-to-paper contact retained over all four flaps after release
Paper tails, not plastic carriers, contact water
Moisture reaches whole sheet including far corners at low reservoir level
Paper material, water level and elapsed wetting times recorded
Poor purchased capillary material is not assumed to work

promotion_rules: Software tests, simulated task success and physical success are distinct
No neural imitation export from failed, privileged-target or incomplete episodes
Never train the robot to force a jam
No use of R3.x, G3 paper liner, snap fits, or printed supports
objective: Make the simulation where the robot assembles and does all G4 planter stages succeed, with independently verified contact-driven motion and complete release/retention.
